title: Mechanic’s View of Aftermarket Car Warranties
summary: A repair shop owner describes how aftermarket warranty claims slow down repairs, get frequently denied, and underpay shops.

assertions.quote: your car will be in my shop longer at least at least double
98% of the warranty companies I've dealt with out there do not cover that initial diagnosis

verdicts.note: Diagnostic-fee exclusions are explicitly listed in vendor contract language elsewhere in this corpus, corroborating the shop's experience beyond a single anecdote.

assertions.quote: 50% or less of the claims we make on our customers behalf are denied

verdicts.note: Denial rates this high are plausible and consistent with other shop and consumer accounts, but this is one shop's unverified estimate, not measured industry data.
FTC found none of CarShield's VSCs covered all repairs or even all repairs to 'covered' systems, due to myriad exclusions, and many consumers had claims denied.

assertions.quote: the fact that the turbo was a non-covered part caused the engine to fail made the whole claim being denied
more than 50% of the time they beat us up over the price

verdicts.note: Reimbursement rate disputes over labor and parts markup are a common, logical consequence of a third-party payer negotiating down a shop's standard billing.
